title: Fair Distribution of Cookies
summary: Given an array of cookie counts per bag and the number of children, find the minimum possible maximum cookies any child can receive by distributing all bags to the children without splitting any bag.
statement: Given an array of cookie counts per bag and the number of children, find the minimum possible maximum cookies any child can receive by distributing all bags to the children without splitting any bag.
constraints: Each bag is indivisible and must be assigned to exactly one of k children.
A child may receive no bag; unfairness is the maximum total assigned to any child.
reference_solution:
def minimum_cookie_unfairness(cookies,k):
    cookies=sorted(cookies,reverse=True);loads=[0]*k;answer=sum(cookies)
    def assign(index):
        nonlocal answer
        if max(loads)>=answer:return
        if index==len(cookies):answer=min(answer,max(loads));return
        seen=set()
        for child in range(k):
            if loads[child] in seen:continue
            seen.add(loads[child]);loads[child]+=cookies[index];assign(index+1);loads[child]-=cookies[index]
            if loads[child]==0:break
    assign(0)
    return answer
hints: Assign larger bags first so bad branches exceed the current bound early.
Backtrack over child loads, pruning when the current maximum cannot beat the best and skipping equal load states.
Try the next bag on each distinct load; undo it, and after the first empty child stop trying other empty children.
Every distinct assignment-load state is explored unless its current maximum already proves it cannot improve the incumbent.
editorial: Every distinct assignment-load state is explored unless its current maximum already proves it cannot improve the incumbent.

tests.explanation: An optimal partition has child totals thirty-one and thirty, so unfairness is thirty-one.
The bags can be divided so the maximum child load is seven.
